subject: Assurance letter: confirmation we don't train on customer data (exceptions & archive clarifications)
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@finsecure.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Assurance request: we are not used for training?

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — FinSecure's legal and security teams are doing a quick sweep of vendor assurances. One item came up in our procurement questionnaire that we need in writing before we can move forward: a firm confirmation that Redwood will not use our customer content to train any ML models or otherwise improve model weights.

Specifically, we need you to address:
- Are any customer inputs (including transcripts, prompt/response pairs, or attachments) used in any model training, fine-tuning, or weight updates?
- Do any backups, debug snapshots, or support artifacts derived from customer requests ever get ingested into training data? If you retain snapshots for debugging, what is the retention window and deletion process?
- Are logs, telemetry, or aggregated usage stats ever used in ways that could alter model behavior?
- Are there any exceptions (legal, safety, aggregated telemetry) where data might be retained longer or used differently?

We need an assurance letter we can share with our internal reviewers and upload to our vendor portal. If you can provide a short attestation and append a short retention appendix with time windows for snapshots/backups/logs, that would be ideal.

Appreciate a quick reply — we are targeting a week for procurement clearance.

Best,
Elena Morales
Senior Counsel, FinSecure
legal@finsecure.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T11:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Assurance request: we are not used for training?

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer content to train model weights, fine-tune our models, or produce derivative models. We can provide a signed assurance letter stating that explicitly.

A few clarifications (high level):
- Training: Customer-provided content (text, audio, attachments) is never included in training datasets or used to update model weights. We do not feed production customer data into any internal training pipelines.
- Telemetry & aggregated stats: We collect telemetry for service reliability (errors, latency), and we may compute aggregated metrics (e.g., average token latency per model). Those aggregated metrics are de-identified and cannot be used to reconstruct customer content. Aggregated telemetry is not material for model training.
- Support snapshots & debug artifacts: For troubleshooting, we retain encrypted request/response snapshots and minimal debug context for up to 7 days by default. These snapshots are accessible to a small set of authorized SRE/Support staff and are deleted automatically unless a customer escalation requires a longer hold; in that case we document the reason, limit access, and delete as soon as the escalation is resolved.
- Backups & disaster recovery: Backups of persistent stores (encrypted at rest) are retained according to our DR policy (typically 30 days) to meet restore objectives. Backups are immutable snapshots of infrastructure state and are not used for training.
- Exceptions: Legal obligations (e.g., court orders) or explicit contractual exceptions (e.g., mutual opt-in to participate in a benchmark program) are the only scenarios where data handling differs, and those would be documented in writing.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short assurance PDF and a retention appendix with the windows above. If you need slightly stronger wording for procurement (e.g., a clause to embed in your vendor portal), we can provide addendum language.

Connor (cc) and Mina, I'm looping you for a one-paragraph technical blurb confirming the 7-day snapshot TTL and the 30-day backup window for the assurance letter. Connor, can you confirm encryption/keys and the process for manual tombstone deletion?

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Head of Legal Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: technical appendix draft for FinSecure assurance

Olga / Connor —

Draft technical text below that I recommend including verbatim in the retention appendix. I've also added an optional sentence about snapshots used during escalations.

--- begin draft ---
Redwood Operational Handling (technical summary):
1) Ephemeral inference state (KV cache): per-request inference KV caches are ephemeral and live only in GPU process memory; they are not persisted to disk and are not present in backups.
2) Debug snapshots: when a customer incident is flagged for investigation, we may create a transient debug snapshot capturing request/response context and selected system logs; default retention for these snapshots is 7 days. Snapshots are encrypted, access-controlled, and are deleted automatically at TTL expiry. If a snapshot needs to be retained for a prolonged investigation, the retention extension is documented in the incident ticket and subject to approval by SRE and Legal.
3) Persistent backups: database and object-store backups used for disaster recovery are retained for up to 30 days, encrypted at rest, and not used for model training. Backups are stored in customer-region buckets per the customer's residency configuration.
4) Aggregation & telemetry: usage metrics and telemetry are aggregated and anonymized for operational monitoring and product analytics. These aggregates cannot be reverse-engineered into customer content and are not used in training pipelines.
5) Deletion & tombstone: upon customer deletion requests, production records are tombstoned and removed from primary stores; we verify deletion from backups during the subsequent backup retention cycle (i.e., data will be purged from backup media within the backup retention window).
--- end draft ---

Connor: can you confirm the encryption/key ownership lines (we use customer-managed KMS for private deployments; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS by default) and whether the 7-day snapshot TTL is currently enforced by an automated job? I believe it is, but would like a confirmation to include in the attestation.

Mina
Director, Product Security (drafting)
From: Elena Morales <elena@finsecure.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: FinSecure Legal <legal@finsecure.com>
Date: 2029-02-14T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Assurance request: we are not used for training?

Olga / team —

Thank you, this is very helpful and addresses the majority of our concerns. Two quick follow-ups: (1) please send the signed assurance PDF and retention appendix to legal@finsecure.com, and (2) please provide a DocuSign or countersignature option so we can store the signed artifact in our vendor system.

If the 7-day snapshot TTL and 30-day backup window are verified in writing, procurement will be able to close this item.

Best regards,
Elena
